options.name: acl
options.setting-help: the access-control lists: who may connect, who may write

options.name: modbus
options.setting-help: the inverter Modbus session: the endpoint, the unit id, the poll plan, the map

options.name: upstream
options.setting-help: the inverter Modbus TCP endpoint HOST:PORT (`:5502` = 127.0.0.1:5502)
options.help: the inverter Modbus TCP endpoint HOST:PORT (`:5502` = 127.0.0.1:5502) (default: config, $UPSTREAM or 127.0.0.1:5502)

options.name: unit
options.setting-help: the Modbus unit id the session speaks
options.help: Modbus unit id (default: config, $UNIT or 1)

options.name: timeout
options.setting-help: upstream Modbus connect/read timeout in seconds
options.help: Modbus connect/read timeout in seconds (default: config, $TIMEOUT or 3)

options.name: interval
options.setting-help: seconds between cache polls of the device
options.help: seconds between cache polls (default: config, $INTERVAL or 10)

options.name: read-delay
options.setting-help: seconds between consecutive device reads within a poll cycle
options.help: seconds between consecutive inverter reads within a poll cycle, 0 = no delay (default: config, $READ_DELAY or 0.05)

options.name: merge-gap
options.setting-help: max register gap when merging ranges into block reads; the plan rebuilds
options.help: max register gap when merging ranges into block reads, 0 = read ranges separately (default: config, $MERGE_GAP or 8)

options.name: cache-ttl
options.setting-help: per-register cache TTL: older entries are refetched

value-help.off: never expire: serve the last known values forever

options.help: per-register cache TTL: cached registers older than this are refetched from the inverter, 0 = never expire, serve last known values forever (default: config, $TTL or 3x interval)

options.name: allow-write
options.setting-help: forward write requests (FC05/06/15/16) to the device

value-help.on: forward writes (the ACLs and the allow-list still gate them)
value-help.off: refuse writes with a Modbus illegal-function exception (the default)

options.help: forward write requests (FC05/06/15/16) to the inverter; default: refuse them with a Modbus illegal-function exception

options.name: write-registers
options.setting-help: the register ranges a write may touch: START:COUNT,...
options.help: register ranges a (forwarded) write may touch: comma-separated START:COUNT, e.g. 47400:100,47600:100; "any" = unrestricted; "none" = no register writable (default: config, $WRITE_REGISTERS or none)

options.name: profile
options.setting-help: device profile JSON: the register ranges to cache (a bare name resolves in profiles/profiles/)
options.help: device profile JSON (the shared profiles/ schema) (default: config, $PROFILE or the bundled sun2000 profile)

options.name: selection
options.setting-help: selection JSON: which profile names to fetch ("all" = every entry, "none" = cache nothing)

value-help.none: cache nothing: the map empties, every read forwards, nothing is stored

options.help: selection JSON: {"registers": ["pv-power", ...]} — the profile names to fetch (default: config, $SELECTION or every profile entry)

options.name: connect-acl
options.setting-help: clients allowed to connect: "any", "none" or comma-separated IPs/prefixes

value-help.none: no client may connect: every connection is rejected

options.help: clients allowed to connect: "any", "none" (refuse everyone) or comma-separated IPs/prefixes like 10.0.0.7,10.48.0.0/16 (default: config, $CONNECT_ACL or any)

options.name: write-acl
options.setting-help: clients allowed to write (requires allow-write): "any", "none" or comma-separated IPs/prefixes

value-help.any: the write gate is allow-write alone

options.help: clients allowed to write (requires --allow-write): "any", "none" (refuse everyone) or comma-separated IPs/prefixes (default: config, $WRITE_ACL or none)

options.name: listen
options.help: listen address HOST:PORT (default: config, $LISTEN or 127.0.0.1:15502)

options.name: local-time
options.setting-help: log timestamps in the system time zone instead of UTC

value-help.on: log timestamps in the system time zone

options.help: log timestamps in the system time zone instead of UTC

options.name: max-clients
options.setting-help: simultaneous client limit
options.help: refuse further connections past this many simultaneous clients, 0 = no limit (default: config, $MAX_CLIENTS or 64)

options.name: client-timeout
options.setting-help: disconnect clients silent for this long
options.help: disconnect clients silent for this many seconds, 0 = never (default: config, $CLIENT_TIMEOUT or 300)

options.name: max-conn-per-ip
options.setting-help: simultaneous connections from one peer IP
options.help: refuse further connections from one peer IP past this many simultaneous connections, 0 = no per-IP limit (default: config, $MAX_CONN_PER_IP or 0)

options.name: control-port
options.help: control server target: unix socket path or TCP port on 127.0.0.1 (default: config, $CTL or /tmp/modbus-cache-<listen-port>.socket); 0 = off

options.name: control-token
options.help: require a token on control connections: the client authenticates with {"cmd": "auth", "token": ...}; over the unix socket a trusted peer (root, the daemon's own user or --control-trust-uids — SO_PEERCRED) skips the token (default: config, $CONTROL_TOKEN or none)

options.name: control-token-file
options.help: the token from a file (the first line; e.g. a systemd LoadCredential or a key file; must be owner-only 0600) — takes the place of --control-token; giving both is an error (default: config, $CONTROL_TOKEN_FILE)

options.name: control-ops-token
options.help: a second, read-only control token: sessions authenticating with it may run the show/clear verbs only (no set/unset, no request dump/restore, no restart, no shutdown) — the ops shift against the admin key, both audited (default: config, $CONTROL_OPS_TOKEN or none)

options.name: control-ops-token-file
options.help: the read-only ops token from a file (the first line; must be owner-only 0600) — takes the place of --control-ops-token; giving both is an error (default: config, $CONTROL_OPS_TOKEN_FILE)

options.name: control-ops-verbs
options.help: the read-only ops role's RBAC policy: the verbs its sessions may run, comma-separated (default: show,clear; validated against the control grammar at start)

options.name: control-trust-uids
options.help: extra peer uids the unix control socket trusts without the token (SO_PEERCRED — a local systemd unit speaks without the secret); root and the daemon's own user are always trusted (default: config, $CONTROL_TRUST_UIDS or none)

options.name: control-socket-group
options.help: leave the unix control socket group-accessible (chmod 0660 instead of the default 0600) (default: config, $CONTROL_SOCKET_GROUP)

options.name: metrics-server
options.setting-help: the cache's own Prometheus /metrics endpoint (needs a token; the address is --metrics-listen)

value-help.on: serve /metrics on the configured listen address

options.help: serve the cache's own Prometheus /metrics endpoint (the live `set metrics-server` toggle exists too); off by default (the default: config, $METRICS_SERVER or off)

options.name: metrics-listen
options.help: the metrics bind address HOST:PORT — 0.0.0.0:PORT serves every interface, a token is mandatory regardless (default: config, $METRICS_LISTEN or 127.0.0.1:9252)

options.name: metrics-token
options.help: require Authorization: Bearer <token> on the /metrics endpoint (the same scheme the scraper speaks)

options.name: metrics-token-file
options.help: the metrics bearer token from a file (the first line; must be owner-only 0600) — takes the place of --metrics-token; giving both is an error (env METRICS_TOKEN_FILE)

options.name: metrics-max-clients
options.help: maximum concurrent HTTP clients on the /metrics endpoint; extras get an immediate 503, 0 = unlimited (default: config, $METRICS_MAX_CLIENTS or 64)

options.name: metrics-client-timeout
options.help: seconds an idle /metrics client is kept before the socket times out, 0 = the built-in 5 s cap (default: config, $METRICS_CLIENT_TIMEOUT or 5)

options.name: metrics-max-conn-per-ip
options.help: maximum concurrent /metrics connections from one peer IP, 0 = no per-IP limit (default: config, $METRICS_MAX_CONN_PER_IP or 0)

options.name: audit-log
options.help: CACHE audit trail: a file path or - for stdout (the docker/journald way); default: config, $AUDIT_LOG or ~/.local/state/modbus-cache/audit.log — the XDG state home

options.name: audit-max-mb
options.help: rotate the audit log at this size in MB, keeping N backups; 0 = no size rotation (default: config, $AUDIT_MAX_MB or 10)

options.name: audit-daily
options.help: also rotate the audit log at UTC midnight (default: config, $AUDIT_DAILY)

options.name: audit-files
options.help: rotated audit backups to keep (default: config, $AUDIT_FILES or 3)

options.name: no-audit-log
options.help: disable the CACHE audit trail (default: config, $NO_AUDIT_LOG)

options.name: requests-audit
options.setting-help: audit one REQUESTS tally per client per this many seconds
options.help: audit one REQUESTS tally per client per this many seconds, 0 = off (default: config, $REQUESTS_AUDIT or 300)

options.name: log-level
options.setting-help: log verbosity
options.help: log level (default: config, $LOG_LEVEL or INFO)

options.name: log-access
options.help: log client connects/disconnects at INFO instead of DEBUG

options.name: dump-path
options.help: the state dump (write-behind): the live setting overrides and — with --dump-with-cache — the cached words, as one JSON, written 0600 with an integrity hash (a restore refuses a tampered, unsigned or group-writable dump); dumped on shutdown, on the request dump command and every --dump-interval seconds; loaded on start only with --restore-on-start, on demand with the request restore command (default: config, $DUMP_PATH or none)

options.name: dump-with-cache
options.help: dump the cached words too: `request dump` and the --dump-interval loop write the words + the settings (the default off = settings only; `request dump with-cache` always includes them; the restore takes either shape) (default: config, $DUMP_WITH_CACHE or off)

options.name: dump-interval
options.setting-help: seconds between the automatic state dumps (the cached words + the setting overrides)

value-help.off: only request dump and the shutdown dump

options.help: seconds between the automatic state dumps, 0 = on request (the request dump command and the shutdown) (default: config, $DUMP_INTERVAL or 0)

options.name: restore-on-start
options.help: load the state dump when the daemon starts (needs --dump-path) — a restart serves last-known values instead of cold misses; default: start cold, load only on demand (default: config, $RESTORE_ON_START)

options.name: limits
options.setting-help: the connection caps: the simultaneous-client and per-IP limits

options.name: write
options.setting-help: the write gates: the forwarding toggle and the register ranges

show.name: status
show.setting-help: multi-line effective state report: one key=value per field

show.name: connections
show.setting-help: connected clients: peer, age, requests served

show.name: cache
show.setting-help: cache contents: ranges, words, freshness, hits/misses

show.name: cache-all
show.setting-help: every cached range-entry: its words, age, expiry and status

show.name: uplink
show.setting-help: the inverter link: session counters, per-block latency and errors

show.name: config
show.setting-help: the effective configuration as a set-grammar script (the secrets are hidden)

show.name: knobs
show.setting-help: the dictionary of all knobs: every knob, its flag, its env twin, its section, how it changes

commands.name: unset
commands.help: restore a setting to its configured value: unset <setting>

commands.name: inspect
commands.help: one pretty dump of everything (the status, the map, the counters, the write gate)

commands.name: request
commands.help: the state dumps (when the daemon has a dump path): request dump / request restore

commands.name: clear
commands.help: drop the cached registers, repoll now (clear cache)

commands.name: restart
commands.help: restart the upstream session: connection + cache dropped, repoll

commands.name: shutdown
commands.help: stop the proxy gracefully (asks to confirm)
